draft.title: The court hierarchy
card: Courts are ranked in a hierarchy. In NSW, a case starts in the Local, District or Supreme Court, depending on how serious it is.
The Local Court hears the least serious matters, which are the most common cases. The District Court hears more serious matters.
The Supreme Court hears the most serious matters in NSW, such as murder.
Federal matters go to federal courts. The High Court of Australia is the highest court in the country.
draft.remember: In NSW, the more serious the case, the higher the court it starts in. The High Court is at the top.

a.q: In NSW, which court would normally hear a charge of murder first?
a.why: Murder is among the most serious matters, so it starts in the Supreme Court. The District Court is the tempting answer because it also hears serious cases, but it hears less serious matters than the Supreme Court.
a.clue: Which NSW court hears the most serious matters?

b.q: Priya is charged with a minor offence in Newcastle. Which court would normally hear the case first?
b.why: Cases start in a court that matches how serious they are, and minor offences are heard in the Local Court. The High Court is the tempting answer because it is the highest court, but it is not where a minor matter begins.
b.clue: The least serious matters start in the lowest court.

problems.detail: In NSW, a murder charge first goes before the Local Court for bail and committal proceedings, and only then to the Supreme Court for trial. A careful teacher could defend 'The Local Court' for 'hear a charge of murder first'. Rewording to 'Which court would normally hold the trial for murder?' would remove the ambiguity.

'A case starts in the Local, District or Supreme Court, depending on how serious it is' simplifies NSW practice: serious indictable offences are first mentioned and committed in the Local Court before trial in the District or Supreme Court. Consider saying serious cases are 'tried' or 'heard' in the higher courts rather than that they 'start' there.

proposal.title: The court hierarchy
card: Courts are ranked in a hierarchy, from lower courts to higher courts. In NSW, the more serious a case is, the higher the court that tries or hears it.
The Local Court hears the least serious matters, such as minor offences, and it handles most cases. The District Court hears more serious matters.
The Supreme Court is the highest court in NSW. It holds the trials for the most serious matters, such as murder.
Many federal matters, such as family law disputes, go to federal courts. The High Court of Australia is the highest court in the country.
proposal.remember: In NSW, the more serious the case, the higher the court that hears it. The High Court is at the top.

b.clue: The least serious matters go to the lowest court.
